concepts.name: Ideal Gas Law Calculations (PV = nRT)
concepts.explanation: Solving for any one variable in PV = nRT given the others, using Kelvin temperature and consistent units.

concepts.name: Combined Gas Law Calculations
concepts.explanation: Applying P1V1/T1 = P2V2/T2 to relate two states of a gas with constant amount of substance, using Kelvin temperature.

concepts.name: Mole-to-Gram Conversion Using Molar Mass
concepts.explanation: Converting amount to mass via m = n × M, where M is molar mass.

concepts.name: Gram-to-Mole Conversion Using Molar Mass
concepts.explanation: Converting mass to amount via n = m / M, where M is molar mass.

concepts.name: Particle-to-Mole Conversion Using Avogadro Constant
concepts.explanation: Computing amount from number of entities via n = N / NA.

concepts.name: Mole-to-Particle Conversion Using Avogadro Constant
concepts.explanation: Computing number of entities from amount via N = n × NA.

concepts.name: Calculating Relative Atomic Mass from Isotopic Abundances
concepts.explanation: Using weighted mean Ar = Σ(isotopic mass × fractional abundance).

concepts.name: Boyle's Law Calculations
concepts.explanation: Applying inverse proportionality P1V1 = P2V2 at constant temperature and amount.

concepts.name: Charles's Law Calculations
concepts.explanation: Applying direct proportionality V1/T1 = V2/T2 at constant pressure and amount (T in Kelvin).

concepts.name: Gay-Lussac's Law Calculations
concepts.explanation: Applying direct proportionality P1/T1 = P2/T2 at constant volume and amount (T in Kelvin).

concepts.name: Charge Balance in Writing Formulas of Ionic Compounds
concepts.explanation: Finding smallest whole-number subscripts so total positive and negative charges sum to zero.

concepts.name: Determining Number of Neutrons from Mass and Atomic Numbers
concepts.explanation: Calculating neutrons using Nn = A − Z.

concepts.name: Determining Electron Count of Ions from Atomic Number and Charge
concepts.explanation: Computing electrons via e− = Z − q for cations and e− = Z + |q| for anions.

concepts.name: Temperature Conversion between Celsius and Kelvin
concepts.explanation: Converting temperatures using K = °C + 273.15.

concepts.name: Direct and Inverse Proportionality in Gas Relationships
concepts.explanation: Recognizing and using y ∝ x and y ∝ 1/x to model V–T and P–V relationships and solve for unknowns.

concepts.name: Stoichiometric Mole Ratio Calculation
concepts.explanation: Using coefficients in a balanced chemical equation to form mole ratios and compute unknown amounts.

concepts.name: Balancing Chemical Equations by Inspection
concepts.explanation: Adjusting stoichiometric coefficients to conserve atoms of each element.

concepts.name: Mass-Mass Stoichiometry
concepts.explanation: Calculating masses of reactants or products using molar mass and mole ratios.

concepts.name: Molarity Calculation (mol per Litre)
concepts.explanation: Computing concentration as moles of solute per litre of solution.

concepts.name: Moles from Molarity and Volume (n = cV)
concepts.explanation: Finding amount of substance using the relation moles = molarity × volume.

concepts.name: Dilution Calculation (C1V1 = C2V2)
concepts.explanation: Relating initial and final concentrations and volumes to compute dilutions.

concepts.name: Percentage Composition by Mass from Chemical Formula
concepts.explanation: Determining each element’s mass fraction and percentage in a compound from its formula.

concepts.name: Empirical Formula Determination from Percent Composition
concepts.explanation: Converting percent by mass to moles, forming simplest whole-number atom ratios.

concepts.name: Empirical Formula from Masses of Reactants and Products
concepts.explanation: Using measured masses to deduce simplest atomic ratio for a compound.

concepts.name: Limiting Reactant Identification
concepts.explanation: Determining which reactant limits product formation by comparing available mole ratios to stoichiometric requirements.

concepts.name: Percentage Yield Calculation
concepts.explanation: Computing reaction efficiency as actual yield divided by theoretical yield times 100%.

concepts.name: Gas Volume Stoichiometry at Specified Conditions
concepts.explanation: Using molar volume at stated conditions to convert between moles and gas volumes in stoichiometric calculations.

concepts.name: Convert Molarity to Grams per Litre
concepts.explanation: Calculating g/L from mol/L using molar mass: g/L = M × molar mass.

concepts.name: Convert Grams per Litre to Molarity
concepts.explanation: Calculating mol/L from g/L using molar mass: M = (g/L) ÷ molar mass.

concepts.name: Standard Solution Mass Calculation
concepts.explanation: Finding the solute mass needed to prepare a target volume at a specified molarity.

concepts.name: Acid-Base Titration Stoichiometry
concepts.explanation: Using titration volumes and stoichiometric ratios to determine unknown concentration.

concepts.name: Solution–Solid Stoichiometry
concepts.explanation: Relating moles in a solution to mass of a reacting solid via the balanced equation.

concepts.name: Parts per Million (ppm) Calculations
concepts.explanation: Computing trace concentration values, e.g., ppm ≈ mg/L for dilute aqueous solutions.

concepts.name: Serial Dilution Factor Computation
concepts.explanation: Determining concentration after sequential dilutions, e.g., 1:10 steps reduce concentration by 10^n.

concepts.name: Redox Titration Stoichiometry (Permanganate–Iron(II))
concepts.explanation: Applying the balanced redox equation or electron-equivalent ratios to compute unknown concentrations.

concepts.name: Oxidation Number Assignment
concepts.explanation: Applying rules to assign oxidation states to atoms in compounds and ions.

concepts.name: Balancing Redox Equations by Half-Reaction Method
concepts.explanation: Separating into oxidation and reduction halves, balancing atoms and charge, and recombining.

concepts.name: Reaction Rate Calculation from Data
concepts.explanation: Computing average rate as change in measurable quantity over time and estimating initial rate from a tangent.

concepts.name: Equilibrium Constant Expression (Kc)
concepts.explanation: Writing Kc in terms of reactant and product concentrations raised to stoichiometric powers.

concepts.name: Equilibrium Concentration Calculations using ICE Tables
concepts.explanation: Setting up initial-change-equilibrium tables to solve for unknown equilibrium concentrations from Kc.

concepts.name: pH Calculation for Strong Acids and Bases
concepts.explanation: Using pH = −log[H+] and pOH = −log[OH−] with full dissociation assumptions.

concepts.name: pH of Weak Acids/Bases using Ka or Kb
concepts.explanation: Setting up equilibrium expressions and approximations to compute pH from Ka or Kb.

concepts.name: Water Autoionization and Kw Relations
concepts.explanation: Using Kw = [H+][OH−] and pH + pOH = 14 at 25°C to interconvert acid-base quantities.

concepts.name: Calorimetry: q = mcΔT
concepts.explanation: Calculating heat change from mass, specific heat capacity, and temperature change; scaling to molar enthalpy.

concepts.name: Enthalpy Change via Hess's Law
concepts.explanation: Algebraic combination of chemical equations and their enthalpy changes to find an unknown ΔH.

concepts.name: Reaction Enthalpy from Bond Enthalpies
concepts.explanation: Estimating ΔH by summing energies of bonds broken minus bonds formed.

concepts.name: Reaction Enthalpy from Standard Enthalpies of Formation
concepts.explanation: Computing ΔH°rxn = ΣνΔH°f(products) − ΣνΔH°f(reactants).

concepts.name: Standard Cell Potential Calculation (E°cell)
concepts.explanation: Determining E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode using standard reduction potentials.

concepts.name: Percentage Error and Precision in Volumetric Results
concepts.explanation: Calculating percent error and assessing accuracy and precision of titration measurements.

concepts.name: Direct Proportionality
concepts.explanation: Understanding relationships of the form y = kx where one quantity increases in direct proportion to another; graph passes through the origin with constant slope.

concepts.name: Inverse Proportionality
concepts.explanation: Recognizing relationships where the product of two quantities is constant (xy = k), so decreasing one increases the other; typical graph is a rectangular hyperbola.

concepts.name: Average Rate Calculation from Experimental Data
concepts.explanation: Computing rate as change in a measured quantity over time, e.g., Δmass/Δtime, using tabulated or graphed experimental results.

concepts.name: Quantitative Data
concepts.explanation: Numerical measurements such as mass, volume, temperature, and time collected with instruments.

concepts.name: Qualitative Data
concepts.explanation: Descriptive observations such as color change, gas evolution, or cloudiness recorded during experiments.

concepts.name: Repeatability of Measurements
concepts.explanation: Assessing whether the same operator using the same method obtains consistent results on repeated trials.

concepts.name: Reproducibility of Results
concepts.explanation: Evaluating whether different operators or laboratories obtain consistent results when following the same procedure.

concepts.name: Reliability of Data
concepts.explanation: Determining consistency of measurements through replication and consistency checks before drawing conclusions.

concepts.name: Using Tables and Graphs to Summarize Data
concepts.explanation: Organizing experimental results into tables and appropriate graphs to reveal patterns and support analysis.

concepts.name: SI Base Units for Length, Mass, and Time
concepts.explanation: Recognizing and using the metre (m), kilogram (kg), and second (s) as standard measurement units.

concepts.name: Measuring Mass, Volume, and Time
concepts.explanation: Selecting instruments and reading measurements for mass, volume, and time to collect quantitative data.

concepts.name: Mathematical Modeling for Prediction
concepts.explanation: Formulating simplified mathematical relationships to explain phenomena and predict outcomes under changed conditions.

concepts.name: Scientific Notation for Very Small Numbers
concepts.explanation: Expressing extremely small quantities like 1.6×10^-19 or 9.1×10^-31 using powers of ten.

concepts.name: Comparing Numbers in Scientific Notation
concepts.explanation: Ordering and comparing magnitudes such as 10^-27 vs 10^-31 by using exponent rules and order-of-magnitude reasoning.

concepts.name: Interpreting Relative Mass Ratios
concepts.explanation: Using given ratios like electron mass = 1/1838 of proton to compare and compute related quantities.

concepts.name: Charge-to-Mass Ratio Calculation
concepts.explanation: Computing or interpreting a ratio such as e/m from measured quantities and understanding its units.

concepts.name: Converting Fractions to Scientific Notation
concepts.explanation: Rewriting fractional scales like 1/100000 as 1×10^-5 for efficient calculation and comparison.

concepts.name: Scale Factor in Models
concepts.explanation: Applying scale factors (e.g., nucleus diameter vs atom diameter) to reason about size comparisons and analogies.

concepts.name: Interpreting Two-Way Tables
concepts.explanation: Reading and comparing categorical numerical information (relative charge, relative mass, location) from a table.

concepts.name: Planck's Relation ΔE = hf
concepts.explanation: Relates the energy difference between atomic levels to the frequency of emitted or absorbed light via Planck's constant.

concepts.name: Speed–Frequency–Wavelength Relation c = fλ
concepts.explanation: The speed of light equals the product of frequency and wavelength for electromagnetic waves.

concepts.name: Photon Energy from Wavelength E = hc/λ
concepts.explanation: Combines Planck's relation with the wave relation to express photon energy as a function of wavelength.

concepts.name: Quantised Energy Levels Indexed by n
concepts.explanation: Electron energies take discrete values labeled by the integer principal quantum number n.

concepts.name: Mapping Electron Transitions to Spectral Frequencies
concepts.explanation: Use ΔE = hf to compute photon frequencies emitted by electron transitions between energy levels.

concepts.name: Determining Energy Level Differences from Measured Wavelength
concepts.explanation: Calculate energy differences between levels from a spectral line's wavelength using ΔE = hc/λ.

concepts.name: Series Identification by Terminal Energy Level (Lyman/Balmer/Paschen)
concepts.explanation: Classify spectral lines by the lower energy level n to which electrons transition, linking to UV, visible, and IR regions.

concepts.name: Orbital as a 95% Probability Region
concepts.explanation: Defines an orbital as the three-dimensional region containing approximately 95% of the electron's probability density.

concepts.name: S-Orbital Spherical Symmetry
concepts.explanation: Model and recognize s orbitals as spheres with radial probability symmetry about the nucleus.

concepts.name: P-Orbital Dumbbell Shape and Orientation (px, py, pz)
concepts.explanation: Represent three orthogonal p orbitals aligned with the x, y, and z axes in 3D space.

concepts.name: Counting Orbitals within Sublevels
concepts.explanation: Determine the number of orbitals in sublevels: s has 1; p has 3 of equal energy.

concepts.name: Measuring Wavelengths with a Spectrometer
concepts.explanation: Acquire quantitative wavelength data from emission spectra using instrumentation.

concepts.name: Discrete vs Continuous Spectra
concepts.explanation: Contrast discrete line spectra with continuous spectra as examples of discrete versus continuous sets of wavelengths.

concepts.name: Convergence of Energy Levels with Increasing n
concepts.explanation: Understand that spacing between successive energy levels decreases as n increases, illustrating a convergent sequence.

concepts.name: Qualitative Uncertainty Principle for Measurement
concepts.explanation: Interpret the limitation on simultaneous precision of position and velocity as a measurement uncertainty concept.

concepts.name: Computing Relative Atomic Mass from Isotopic Abundances
concepts.explanation: Calculate an element’s relative atomic mass as the weighted mean of its isotopes using their masses and percentage abundances.

concepts.name: Building Electron Configurations with the Aufbau Principle
concepts.explanation: Construct the s, p, d electron configuration by filling sublevels from lowest to highest energy (including 4s before 3d) for atoms and simple ions.

concepts.name: Applying Hund's Rule to Distribute Electrons Among Degenerate Orbitals
concepts.explanation: Place electrons singly into orbitals of equal energy before pairing to maximize unpaired electrons.

concepts.name: Applying the Pauli Exclusion Principle to Orbital Occupancy
concepts.explanation: Enforce a maximum of two electrons per orbital with opposite spins when assigning electrons.

concepts.name: Using 2n^2 Formula for Maximum Electrons per Shell
concepts.explanation: Evaluate the capacity of a main energy level n using the formula 2n^2 (e.g., n=1→2, n=2→8, n=3→18).

concepts.name: Determining Electron Configuration via Periodic Table Shell Counts (Bohr Model)
concepts.explanation: Allocate electrons across shells by counting positions across periods to produce configurations like 2,8,8,1.

concepts.name: Determining Electron Count of Ions from Charge
concepts.explanation: Find the number of electrons in an ion by adding for negative charge and subtracting for positive charge from the atomic number.

concepts.name: Counting Occupied Orbitals from an Electron Configuration
concepts.explanation: Given an s, p, d configuration, count the number of orbitals used using sublevel degeneracies (s:1, p:3, d:5).

concepts.name: Calculating Neutrons from Nuclear Symbol (A and Z)
concepts.explanation: Compute neutron number as mass number minus atomic number using A/Z notation.

concepts.name: Converting Percentage Abundances to Weighted Counts
concepts.explanation: Translate percentage composition into counts (e.g., out of 100) to compute weighted averages such as atomic masses.

concepts.name: Rounding Relative Atomic Mass to the Nearest Whole Number
concepts.explanation: Round a decimal atomic weight to the nearest integer to estimate a mass number for calculations.

concepts.name: Scientific Notation for Very Small Masses
concepts.explanation: Represent and interpret extremely small quantities such as the atomic mass unit using scientific notation (e.g., 1.66×10^-24 g).

concepts.name: Periodicity in Ordered Sequences
concepts.explanation: Recognize and reason about properties that repeat at regular intervals in an ordered list, a concept of periodic patterns.

concepts.name: Interpreting Electron Configuration Exponents as Counts
concepts.explanation: Read notations like 2p^6 as indicating the number of electrons in a sublevel, interpreting exponents as counts rather than powers.

concepts.name: Charge Balance to Determine Ionic Formula
concepts.explanation: Set the sum of positive and negative ion charges to zero and choose subscripts so the overall compound is electrically neutral.

concepts.name: Using Least Common Multiple for Ionic Formulas
concepts.explanation: Use the LCM of ion charge magnitudes to find the smallest whole-number ratio of ions (e.g., Al3+ and O2− form Al2O3).

concepts.name: Interpreting Subscripts as Ratios in Chemical Formulas
concepts.explanation: Read subscripts to determine the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms or ions in a compound (e.g., Na2S is 2:1).

concepts.name: Counting Valence Electrons for VSEPR
concepts.explanation: Sum valence electrons from the central and surrounding atoms to find the total electron pairs that determine molecular geometry.

concepts.name: Mapping Four Electron Pairs to Tetrahedral Geometry
concepts.explanation: Recognize that four electron pairs around a central atom lead to tetrahedral electron-pair geometry.

concepts.name: Lone Pair Repulsion Effect on Bond Angles
concepts.explanation: Account for stronger lone pair–bond pair repulsions that reduce bond angles from the ideal geometry (e.g., 109.5° to about 107° or 104.5°).

concepts.name: Identifying Trigonal Pyramidal Shape (AX3E)
concepts.explanation: Three bond pairs and one lone pair on the central atom yield a trigonal pyramidal molecular shape with bond angles near 107°.

concepts.name: Identifying Bent (V-Shaped) Shape (AX2E2)
concepts.explanation: Two bond pairs and two lone pairs on the central atom yield a bent shape with bond angles near 104.5°.

concepts.name: Identifying Linear Molecular Shape (AX2)
concepts.explanation: Two bonding regions and no lone pairs around a central atom produce a linear molecule with a 180° bond angle.

concepts.name: Counting Sigma and Pi Bonds in Multiple Bonds
concepts.explanation: Classify single bonds as sigma; double bonds as one sigma plus one pi; triple bonds as one sigma plus two pi, and count accordingly.

concepts.name: Writing Net Ionic Equations for Precipitation
concepts.explanation: Represent only reacting ions and the precipitate, balancing atoms and charge, and denote the precipitate with a downward arrow.

concepts.name: Using Parentheses for Polyatomic Ion Multiplicity
concepts.explanation: Apply parentheses with subscripts to indicate multiple copies of a polyatomic ion in formulas (e.g., Ca(HCO3)2).

concepts.name: Determining Formulas from Oxidation State Notation
concepts.explanation: Use Roman numerals to set the ion’s charge and match with counter-ion charges to deduce the empirical formula.

concepts.name: Unit Cell and Crystal Lattice Repetition
concepts.explanation: Understand the unit cell as a repeating 3D spatial pattern that tessellates to form a crystal lattice.

concepts.name: Tetrahedral Angle 109.5 Degrees
concepts.explanation: Recognize and apply the ideal 109.5° bond angle for tetrahedral arrangements in shape predictions.

concepts.name: Electronegativity Difference (Absolute Value) Calculation
concepts.explanation: Compute the absolute difference between two electronegativity values to quantify bond polarity.

concepts.name: Bond Type Prediction Using Inequality Thresholds
concepts.explanation: Apply piecewise numerical thresholds on electronegativity difference to classify bonds as pure covalent (Δ=0), slightly polar (0<Δ≤0.4), polar covalent (0.4<Δ<1.7), or ionic (Δ>1.7).

concepts.name: Vector Addition of Bond Dipoles to Determine Molecular Polarity
concepts.explanation: Model bond dipoles as vectors and compute the resultant to decide if a molecule has a net dipole moment.

concepts.name: Symmetry-Induced Cancellation of Net Dipole
concepts.explanation: Use molecular symmetry to infer that symmetric arrangements cause dipole vectors to cancel, yielding a net dipole of zero.

concepts.name: Trend Analysis from Line Graphs and Tables
concepts.explanation: Interpret monotonic trends (e.g., boiling point vs atomic number or molecular size) from graphical and tabular data.

concepts.name: Ratio and Percentage Comparison of Interaction Strengths
concepts.explanation: Compare magnitudes using ratios and percentages (e.g., hydrogen bonds ≈10% of covalent strength; dispersion ≈0.1%).

concepts.name: Inclusive vs Strict Inequality Interpretation in Classification Rules
concepts.explanation: Correctly interpret boundary conditions such as ≤, <, and compound inequalities when applying piecewise rules.

concepts.name: Ranking Substances by Numerical Property
concepts.explanation: Order and compare entities based on numerical measures such as boiling point to support claims about intermolecular forces.

concepts.name: Sum-to-Zero Constraint for Net Quantity
concepts.explanation: Model neutrality constraints where signed quantities sum to zero (e.g., total partial charges in a neutral molecule).

concepts.name: Effective Nuclear Charge Calculation (Z_eff = Z − S)
concepts.explanation: Compute the net positive charge attracting valence electrons by subtracting the shielding effect S from the nuclear charge Z.

concepts.name: Covalent Radius from Bond Length
concepts.explanation: Determine an element’s covalent (atomic) radius as half the distance between nuclei in a homonuclear single bond: r = d/2.

concepts.name: Interpreting Ionisation Energy vs Atomic Number Graphs
concepts.explanation: Read and analyze plots of first ionisation energy against atomic number to identify periodic trends and recognize exceptions.

concepts.name: Logarithmic Scaling of Ionisation Energy Data
concepts.explanation: Apply and interpret logarithmic transformations to compress wide-ranging ionisation energy values for graphical analysis.

concepts.name: Successive Ionisation Energy Jump Analysis
concepts.explanation: Identify large jumps in successive ionisation energies to infer electron shell and sublevel boundaries from data sequences.

concepts.name: Interpreting Electronegativity vs Atomic Number Graphs
concepts.explanation: Analyze electronegativity plots to determine increasing trends across periods and decreasing trends down groups.

concepts.name: Unit Rate Interpretation of Energy Values (kJ per mol)
concepts.explanation: Interpret and work with per-mole energy units (kJ mol⁻¹), recognizing equivalent forms such as kJ/mol.

concepts.name: Converting Grams to Moles Using n = m/M
concepts.explanation: Compute the number of moles by dividing the sample mass by the molar mass.

concepts.name: Converting Moles to Grams Using m = nM
concepts.explanation: Find the mass of a substance by multiplying the number of moles by the molar mass.

concepts.name: Calculating Relative Molecular Mass from Chemical Formula
concepts.explanation: Sum the relative atomic masses of all atoms in the formula, accounting for subscripts and multiplicities.

concepts.name: Calculating Molar Mass and Units g mol^-1
concepts.explanation: Express the mass of one mole of a substance in grams per mole, derived from atomic or molecular masses.

concepts.name: Using Formula Subscripts as Multiplicative Factors in Mass Calculations
concepts.explanation: Interpret subscripts in chemical formulas to multiply atomic masses appropriately (e.g., O2, SO4^2-, hydrates).

concepts.name: Computing Number of Particles from Moles Using N = n·NA
concepts.explanation: Multiply moles by Avogadro’s constant to obtain the number of entities (atoms, molecules, or formula units).

concepts.name: Computing Moles from Number of Particles Using n = N/NA
concepts.explanation: Divide the number of entities by Avogadro’s constant to determine moles.

concepts.name: Computing Number of Particles from Mass Using N = (m/M)·NA
concepts.explanation: Convert mass to moles and then to particles in a single calculation.

concepts.name: Computing Mass from Number of Particles Using m = (N/NA)·M
concepts.explanation: Convert entities to moles and then to mass in a single formula.

concepts.name: Scientific Notation Operations with Avogadro-scale Quantities
concepts.explanation: Perform multiplication and division with numbers in scientific notation when using Avogadro’s constant.

concepts.name: Ratio and Proportion Method for Mole Calculations
concepts.explanation: Use unitary methods or proportional reasoning to scale between known mass–particle relationships.

concepts.name: Dimensional Analysis for Mole–Mass–Particles Conversions
concepts.explanation: Track and cancel units systematically to ensure correct conversion between grams, moles, and particles.

concepts.name: Applying the Ideal Gas Equation (PV = nRT)
concepts.explanation: Solve for an unknown variable in PV=nRT while maintaining consistent SI units (Pa, m^3, K, mol).

concepts.name: Using the Combined Gas Law
concepts.explanation: Compute unknown pressure, volume, or temperature with p1V1/T1 = p2V2/T2, converting temperatures to kelvins.

concepts.name: Boyle's Law: Inverse Proportionality of Pressure and Volume
concepts.explanation: Model p ∝ 1/V at constant temperature and use pV = constant for calculations.

concepts.name: Charles' Law: Direct Proportionality of Volume and Temperature (Kelvin)
concepts.explanation: Use V ∝ T (in kelvins) at constant pressure and apply V/T = constant.

concepts.name: Avogadro's Law and Molar Volume at STP
concepts.explanation: Apply V ∝ n under fixed T and p and use molar volume 22.4 L mol⁻¹ at STP.

concepts.name: Celsius–Kelvin Temperature Conversion
concepts.explanation: Convert temperatures via T(K) = T(°C) + 273 for use in gas law calculations.

concepts.name: Volume Unit Conversion to Cubic Metres
concepts.explanation: Convert cm³ and litres to m³ using 1 L = 10⁻³ m³ and 1 cm³ = 10⁻⁶ m³; 1 m³ = 10⁶ cm³.

concepts.name: Pressure Unit Conversion to Pascals
concepts.explanation: Convert between Pa, kPa, and hPa; use 1 kPa = 1000 Pa and 1 hPa = 100 Pa.

concepts.name: Calculating Gas Density from Molar Volume
concepts.explanation: Use density = molar mass / molar volume, e.g., at STP density = Mr / 22.4 L.

concepts.name: Determining Relative Molecular Mass from Gas Data
concepts.explanation: Find molar mass using measured mass and moles computed from PV=nRT for a gas sample.

concepts.name: Gay-Lussac's Law of Combining Volumes
concepts.explanation: Use simple whole-number ratios of reacting and product gas volumes at the same T and p.

concepts.name: Linearization for Boyle's Law (Plotting p vs 1/V)
concepts.explanation: Demonstrate inverse proportionality by plotting pressure against reciprocal volume to obtain a straight line through the origin.

concepts.name: Using Standard Temperature and Pressure in Gas Calculations
concepts.explanation: Apply STP (T=273 K, p≈1.013×10⁵ Pa) to compare gas volumes and use molar volume appropriately.

concepts.name: Calculating Moles from Mass and Molar Mass
concepts.explanation: Compute amount of substance via n = mass / molar mass to use within gas law formulas.

concepts.name: Identifying Linear V–T(K) Relationship
concepts.explanation: Plot volume against absolute temperature to verify direct proportionality predicted by Charles' Law.

concepts.name: Conservation of Mass in Stoichiometric Calculations
concepts.explanation: Using the principle that total mass of reactants equals total mass of products to find unknown masses in reactions.

concepts.name: Balancing Chemical Equations by Atom Counting
concepts.explanation: Ensuring equal counts of each element on both sides by adjusting integer coefficients.

concepts.name: Mass–Mole Conversion Using Molar Mass
concepts.explanation: Converting between grams and moles with molar mass to quantify substances.

concepts.name: Using Stoichiometric Coefficients as Mole Ratios
concepts.explanation: Interpreting balanced equation coefficients to form proportional relationships between substances.

concepts.name: Percentage Composition Calculation from Chemical Formula
concepts.explanation: Computing each element’s mass percentage using atomic masses and the compound’s formula.

concepts.name: Empirical Formula Determination from Percentage Composition
concepts.explanation: Converting mass percentages to moles, forming simplest whole-number ratios to obtain the empirical formula.

concepts.name: Molecular Formula Determination from Empirical Formula and Molar Mass
concepts.explanation: Using n = Mr / (empirical formula mass) to scale the empirical formula to the molecular formula.

concepts.name: Empirical Formula from Mass Data via Gravimetric Analysis
concepts.explanation: Using measured masses of reactants/products and conservation of mass to compute atom ratios and infer the empirical formula.

concepts.name: Stoichiometric Mass–Mass Calculations from Balanced Equations
concepts.explanation: Determining product or reactant masses by chaining mass–mole conversion and mole ratios.

concepts.name: Gas Volume Calculation at STP Using Molar Volume
concepts.explanation: Using 22.4 L per mole at STP to convert between moles and gas volumes in reactions.

concepts.name: Particle–Mole Conversion Using Avogadro’s Constant
concepts.explanation: Relating numbers of molecules/atoms to moles via 6.02×10^23.

concepts.name: Determining Water of Crystallisation from Mass Loss
concepts.explanation: Finding the value of x in hydrated salts by comparing mass before and after heating to dryness.

concepts.name: Dimensional Analysis in Stoichiometry
concepts.explanation: Systematically converting units (e.g., kg↔g, moles↔grams↔molecules) to maintain consistency in calculations.

concepts.name: Balancing Chemical Equations by Atom Conservation
concepts.explanation: Adjust integer coefficients so that the count of each element is equal on both sides of a reaction, satisfying conservation of mass.

concepts.name: Writing Net Ionic Equations by Canceling Spectator Ions
concepts.explanation: Derive the net ionic form of a reaction by removing ions that appear unchanged on both sides of the equation.

concepts.name: Stoichiometric Ratios in Acid–Base Neutralisation
concepts.explanation: Use mole ratios of H+ and OH− (including polyprotic acids) to determine coefficients and products in neutralisation reactions.

concepts.name: Charge Balance in Ionic Reaction Equations
concepts.explanation: Ensure the algebraic sum of charges is conserved across reactants and products when balancing ionic reactions.

concepts.name: Clearing Fractional Coefficients to Obtain Least Whole-Number Balance
concepts.explanation: Solve for fractional coefficients and scale by the least common multiple to obtain the smallest integer set of coefficients.

concepts.name: Interpreting Coefficients vs Subscripts in Chemical Formulas
concepts.explanation: Differentiate between equation coefficients (scaling quantities) and formula subscripts (fixed composition) to count atoms correctly.

concepts.name: Counting Transferable Protons to Determine Acid Basicity
concepts.explanation: Identify monoprotic, diprotic, and triprotic acids by counting dissociable protons to predict neutralisation stoichiometry.

concepts.name: Using Reaction Templates for Acid–Carbonate Equations
concepts.explanation: Apply the pattern Acid + Carbonate → Salt + Water + CO2 and then balance using stoichiometric coefficients.

concepts.name: Titration Stoichiometry: VaMa/na = VbMb/nb
concepts.explanation: At equivalence, the stoichiometric moles of acid and base are equal; volumes, molarities, and coefficients satisfy Va·Ma/na = Vb·Mb/nb.

concepts.name: Molarity (mol per litre)
concepts.explanation: Concentration defined as moles of solute per litre of solution; 1 M means 1 mol in 1 L.

concepts.name: Calculating Moles from Volume and Molarity
concepts.explanation: Compute amount of substance using n = M·V (with V in litres) or n = (V_cm3·M)/1000.

concepts.name: Dilution Calculation using M1V1 = M2V2
concepts.explanation: Use conservation of moles on dilution to relate concentrations and volumes before and after: M1V1 = M2V2.

concepts.name: Converting Molarity to Grams per Litre
concepts.explanation: Find g/L from molarity using g/L = M · Mr, where Mr is molar mass (g/mol).

concepts.name: Converting Grams per Litre to Molarity
concepts.explanation: Compute molarity from mass concentration using M = (g/L) / Mr.

concepts.name: Percentage Concentration by Mass (w/w)
concepts.explanation: Compute percent mass of solute per mass of solution: % w/w = (mass solute / total mass solution) × 100.

concepts.name: Percentage Concentration by Mass/Volume (w/v)
concepts.explanation: Compute grams of solute per 100 cm³ of solution: % w/v = (g solute / 100 cm³ solution) × 100.

concepts.name: Percentage Concentration by Volume (v/v)
concepts.explanation: Compute volume of solute per 100 cm³ of solution: % v/v = (volume solute / total volume solution) × 100.

concepts.name: Parts per Million (ppm) as mg/L
concepts.explanation: For dilute aqueous solutions, 1 ppm equals 1 mg per litre; convert between ppm and mg/L.

concepts.name: Serial Dilution with Fixed Dilution Factor
concepts.explanation: Compute successive concentrations by multiplying by the dilution factor each step, e.g., 1:10 gives powers of 1/10.
concepts.broader_concept: Ratio and Proportional Reasoning in Solutions

concepts.name: Mass of Solid Reacting with Solution Volume
concepts.explanation: Determine mass of a solid that reacts with a given solution volume by converting volume to moles, applying mole ratios, then moles to mass.

concepts.name: Computing Relative Molecular Mass from Atomic Masses
concepts.explanation: Calculate Mr by summing relative atomic masses according to the chemical formula.

concepts.name: Averaging Concordant Titre Values
concepts.explanation: Compute the mean of concordant titration volumes (agreeing within 0.1 cm³), excluding the rough trial.

concepts.name: Volume Unit Conversion (cm³, mL, L)
concepts.explanation: Convert between common volume units used in solution work: 1 cm³ = 1 mL; 1000 mL = 1 L.

concepts.name: Titration Proportion Formula (Va×Ma/na = Vb×Mb/nb)
concepts.explanation: Relating volumes and molarities of two reacting solutions using stoichiometric coefficients to solve for an unknown concentration.

concepts.name: Moles from Volume and Molarity (n = V×M/1000)
concepts.explanation: Calculating the amount of substance from a solution’s volume in cm3 and molarity in mol/L using n = V×M/1000.

concepts.name: Moles from Mass (n = m/Mr)
concepts.explanation: Finding the number of moles from a given mass and relative molecular mass, with rearrangement to find mass or Mr.

concepts.name: Using Mole Ratios from a Balanced Equation
concepts.explanation: Extracting stoichiometric coefficients from a balanced equation to relate moles of reactants and products (e.g., 1:1, 1:2, 1:3).

concepts.name: Dilution Factor and Concentration Scaling
concepts.explanation: Calculating concentration changes upon dilution using factor V2/V1 or the relation C1V1 = C2V2.

concepts.name: Converting Grams per Litre to Percent w/v
concepts.explanation: Transforming g/L to percent w/v by expressing grams per 100 cm3 (g per 100 mL).

concepts.name: Calculating Relative Molecular Mass from Atomic Masses
concepts.explanation: Summing tabulated atomic masses to obtain the relative molecular mass of a compound.

concepts.name: Unit Conversion between cm3 and Litres
concepts.explanation: Converting 1000 cm3 to 1 L (and vice versa) to ensure consistent units in solution calculations.

concepts.name: Calculating Moles per Cubic Centimetre from Molarity
concepts.explanation: Converting mol/L to mol/cm3 by dividing by 1000 to obtain moles per cm3.

concepts.name: Density Formula Manipulation (ρ = m/V)
concepts.explanation: Using density to compute mass from volume or volume from mass via proportional relationships.

concepts.name: Classifying Results as Accurate or Precise
concepts.explanation: Determining whether measurements are close to the true value (accuracy) and/or close to each other (precision).

concepts.name: Assessing Precision from Repeated Measurements
concepts.explanation: Evaluating consistency by checking the spread of repeated readings and tolerance criteria.

concepts.name: Percentage Error in Volume Measurement
concepts.explanation: Quantifying and interpreting percent error in measured volumes and its impact on calculated concentrations.

concepts.name: Significant Figures and Rounding in Quantitative Calculations
concepts.explanation: Applying appropriate significant figures and rounding rules when reporting computed concentrations and masses.

concepts.name: Balancing Redox Equations Using Oxidation Numbers
concepts.explanation: A systematic procedure: assign oxidation numbers, determine electrons lost and gained, choose coefficients so total electrons lost equals total electrons gained, then balance remaining atoms (often H and O) and verify atoms and net charge.

concepts.name: Identifying Oxidation and Reduction via Oxidation Number Change
concepts.explanation: Determine which species is oxidised (increase in oxidation number) and which is reduced (decrease in oxidation number).

concepts.name: Assigning Oxidation Numbers in Compounds and Ions
concepts.explanation: Apply standard rules and electronegativity conventions to assign oxidation numbers to atoms in molecules and polyatomic ions.

concepts.name: Electron Transfer Ratio and LCM in Redox Balancing
concepts.explanation: Determine stoichiometric coefficients by equating total electrons lost and gained using the least common multiple of electron changes.
concepts.broader_concept: Balancing Redox Equations Using Oxidation Numbers

concepts.name: Conservation Check of Atoms and Net Charge in Ionic Equations
concepts.explanation: Verify that a balanced equation conserves the count of each atom and the total charge on both sides.

concepts.name: Determining Oxidising and Reducing Agents from Electron Flow
concepts.explanation: Use electron bookkeeping to identify the oxidising agent (species reduced; gains electrons) and the reducing agent (species oxidised; loses electrons).

concepts.name: Spectator Ion Elimination in Redox Analysis
concepts.explanation: Remove ions that do not change oxidation state to focus analysis on the species undergoing oxidation or reduction.

concepts.name: Oxidation Number Rule: Uncombined Element is Zero
concepts.explanation: Any element in its standard uncombined form has oxidation number 0, e.g., H2, O2, Na(s).

concepts.name: Oxidation Number Rule: Monatomic Ion Equals Its Charge
concepts.explanation: For single-atom ions, the oxidation number is identical to the ionic charge, e.g., Fe2+ is +2, Cl− is −1.

concepts.name: Oxidation Number Rule: Sum in Neutral Compound is Zero
concepts.explanation: The algebraic sum of oxidation numbers of all atoms in a neutral compound must be zero.

concepts.name: Oxidation Number Rule: Sum in Polyatomic Ion Equals Ion Charge
concepts.explanation: The sum of oxidation numbers in a polyatomic ion equals the net ionic charge.

concepts.name: Oxidation Number Rule: Oxygen is −2 (Peroxides −1, OF2 +2)
concepts.explanation: Assign O as −2 generally; use −1 in peroxides and +2 in oxygen difluoride due to fluorine’s higher electronegativity.

concepts.name: Oxidation Number Rule: Hydrogen is +1 (Metal Hydrides −1)
concepts.explanation: Hydrogen is +1 in most compounds but −1 in metal hydrides such as NaH.

concepts.name: Oxidation Number Rule: Halogens −1 Unless with More Electronegative Atom
concepts.explanation: Halogens are assigned −1 in compounds except when bonded to a more electronegative element (e.g., O or F), where their oxidation number can be positive.

concepts.name: Electronegativity-Based Assignment in Binary Compounds
concepts.explanation: In binary covalent compounds, assign bonding electrons to the more electronegative element to deduce oxidation numbers.

concepts.name: Average Oxidation Number in Mixed-Valence Compounds
concepts.explanation: Compute the average oxidation number for an element occurring in multiple oxidation states within the same species (e.g., thiosulfate and tetrathionate).

concepts.name: Titration stoichiometry formula (Vo·Mo/no = Vr·Mr/nr)
concepts.explanation: Relates volumes, molarities, and stoichiometric coefficients of oxidising and reducing agents to solve redox titration problems.

concepts.name: Determining mole ratios from half-reactions
concepts.explanation: Using electron balance in oxidation and reduction half-equations to deduce stoichiometric ratios between reactants.

concepts.name: Calculating molarity from titration data
concepts.explanation: Finding the unknown concentration of a solution using measured titration volumes and balanced reaction coefficients.

concepts.name: Converting molarity (mol/L) to mass concentration (g/L)
concepts.explanation: Multiplying molarity by molar mass to express concentration in grams per litre.

concepts.name: Volume unit conversion between cm³ and L
concepts.explanation: Converting millilitre or cubic centimetre volumes to litres (1000 cm³ = 1 L) for use in concentration calculations.

concepts.name: Determining waters of crystallization from titration data
concepts.explanation: Using molar mass computed from titration-derived moles and sample mass to solve for x in hydrated salts (e.g., FeSO4·xH2O).

concepts.name: Balancing redox equations by the half-reaction method
concepts.explanation: Separating into oxidation and reduction half-reactions, balancing atoms and charges with H+, H2O, and e−, then combining.

concepts.name: Assigning oxidation numbers
concepts.explanation: Applying rules to determine oxidation states for elements in compounds to track electron transfer.

concepts.name: Stoichiometric linking across sequential reactions
concepts.explanation: Combining balanced reactions to derive overall equivalences (e.g., 2 MnO4− ≡ 5 I2 ≡ 10 S2O3²−) for multi-step titrations.

concepts.name: Calculating solute mass in an aliquot
concepts.explanation: Using concentration and aliquot volume to find mass of solute in a measured portion of solution.

concepts.name: Computing the mean of replicate titration readings
concepts.explanation: Averaging concordant titres to reduce random error and report a central estimate.

concepts.name: Burette meniscus reading to the nearest 0.05–0.1 cm³
concepts.explanation: Reading the appropriate part of the meniscus at eye level and recording to the instrument’s resolution.

concepts.name: Agreement criterion for concordant titres
concepts.explanation: Applying a tolerance (e.g., within 0.1 cm³) to decide when replicate titration volumes are sufficiently consistent.

concepts.name: Titration Stoichiometric Relation (C1 V1 / n1 = C2 V2 / n2)
concepts.explanation: At the equivalence point, the ratio of moles to stoichiometric coefficient is equal for reactant pairs, enabling calculation of unknown concentration or volume.

concepts.name: Mole Calculation from Mass (n = m / Mr)
concepts.explanation: Compute the number of moles by dividing a substance’s mass by its relative molecular mass; rearrange to find mass or Mr as needed.

concepts.name: Mole Calculation from Volume and Molarity (n = V_cm3 × M / 1000)
concepts.explanation: Calculate moles from a solution’s molarity and a measured volume in cm³ by converting to liters.

concepts.name: Using Balanced-Equation Mole Ratios
concepts.explanation: Use stoichiometric coefficients from a balanced equation to convert between moles of reactants and products.

concepts.name: Concentration Conversion: Molarity to g/L (g/L = M × Mr)
concepts.explanation: Convert between molarity and grams per liter using molar mass for solution composition problems.

concepts.name: Unit Conversion Between cm³ and Liters
concepts.explanation: Convert volumes between cm³ and liters (1 L = 1000 cm³) in solution and titration calculations.

concepts.name: Proportional Scaling of Concentration from First Principles
concepts.explanation: Use direct proportion to scale concentrations and amounts, e.g., deriving molarity from mass in a non-1 L volume without memorized formulas.

concepts.name: Solving for Unknown Concentration in Titration Equations
concepts.explanation: Algebraically isolate the unknown molarity in linear proportional equations derived from titration data.

concepts.name: Averaging Repeated Measurements to Reduce Random Error
concepts.explanation: Compute the mean of concordant titration values to mitigate random fluctuations and improve estimate stability.

concepts.name: Identifying Systematic vs Random Error
concepts.explanation: Classify errors as bias (consistent shift) versus variability (scatter) and anticipate their effects on results.

concepts.name: Accuracy versus Precision
concepts.explanation: Differentiate closeness to the true value (accuracy) from repeatability or spread of measurements (precision).

concepts.name: Concordant Titration Criterion (within 0.1 cm³)
concepts.explanation: Apply an acceptance threshold for agreement between titers to justify averaging and reporting results.

concepts.name: Density Relation (ρ = m / V) and Rearrangement
concepts.explanation: Use the ratio of mass to volume to compute density or rearrange to find mass or volume in solution problems.

concepts.name: Average Reaction Rate from Total Change over Time
concepts.explanation: Compute the average rate as change in a measured quantity (e.g., concentration or volume) divided by the elapsed time over an interval.

concepts.name: Instantaneous Reaction Rate via Tangent Slope
concepts.explanation: Estimate the reaction rate at a specific time by drawing a tangent to the curve and calculating its slope at that point.

concepts.name: Initial Reaction Rate at t=0 from Tangent
concepts.explanation: Determine the initial rate by drawing a tangent at the origin of the product-vs-time or reactant-vs-time curve and finding its slope.

concepts.name: Estimating Instantaneous Rate with Secant Approximation
concepts.explanation: Approximate the tangent slope at a given time by using a nearby secant line through two points on the curve straddling the time of interest.

concepts.name: Calculating Slope as Rise over Run
concepts.explanation: Compute slope by dividing the change in the vertical axis by the change in the horizontal axis between two chosen points.

concepts.name: Direct Proportionality Between Rate and Concentration
concepts.explanation: Recognize and model linear relationships through the origin (rate ∝ concentration) and interpret the slope as the proportionality constant.

concepts.name: Using Reciprocal of Time as Rate Measure (1/t)
concepts.explanation: Use the reciprocal of measured time as a proxy for reaction rate when a fixed extent of reaction marks completion (e.g., obscuring a cross).

concepts.name: Inverse Proportionality Between Time and Rate
concepts.explanation: Interpret that time to reach a fixed event is inversely proportional to the reaction rate (doubling rate halves time).

concepts.name: Plotting Experimental Data with Axes, Units, and Scales
concepts.explanation: Represent tabulated measurements on Cartesian axes with correct labels, units, and scaling to analyze trends.

concepts.name: Identifying Reaction Completion from Graph Plateaus
concepts.explanation: Detect when the rate approaches zero from a volume- or mass-vs-time curve leveling off, indicating no further change.

concepts.name: Activation Energy from Energy Profile Diagram (Vertical Difference)
concepts.explanation: Read activation energy as the vertical energy difference between reactants and the peak (activated complex) on an energy vs reaction coordinate graph.

concepts.name: Comparing Catalysed and Uncatalysed Energy Profiles
concepts.explanation: Analyze two energy profiles to see that a catalyst lowers the activation energy while leaving overall energy change unchanged.

concepts.name: Interpreting ΔH on Energy Profile Diagrams
concepts.explanation: Determine whether a reaction is exothermic or endothermic from relative product and reactant energy levels and read ΔH as their difference.

concepts.name: Interpreting Area Above Threshold in Maxwell–Boltzmann Distribution
concepts.explanation: Use area under a probability density curve above a threshold to represent the fraction of particles exceeding a required energy.

concepts.name: Temperature Effect on Distribution and Threshold Exceedance
concepts.explanation: Qualitatively analyze how increasing temperature shifts a distribution to increase the area above a fixed energy threshold.

concepts.name: Multiplicative Rate Change per Fixed Temperature Increment
concepts.explanation: Model rules like 'rate doubles per 10°C' as a multiplicative factor per fixed step, an example of exponential-type dependence.

concepts.name: Working with Compound Units for Rates
concepts.explanation: Express and interpret rates using compound units such as cm^3/min or mol L^-1 s^-1, including unit conversions when needed.

concepts.name: Writing Equilibrium Constant Expressions (Kc)
concepts.explanation: Formulating Kc by multiplying product concentrations divided by reactant concentrations, each raised to their stoichiometric coefficients.

concepts.name: Calculating Kc from Equilibrium Concentrations
concepts.explanation: Substituting measured equilibrium molarities into the Kc expression to compute the numerical value of the equilibrium constant.

concepts.name: Finding Equilibrium Concentrations from Kc (ICE Method)
concepts.explanation: Using Initial-Change-Equilibrium tables and algebra to solve for unknown equilibrium concentrations consistent with a given Kc.

concepts.name: Units of Kc via Dimensional Analysis
concepts.explanation: Determining the units of Kc by substituting concentration units into the Kc expression and simplifying exponents.

concepts.name: Transformations of Equilibrium Constants
concepts.explanation: Adjusting K when a reaction is reversed (K' = 1/K) or multiplied by a factor (K' = K^n), consistent with equation scaling.

concepts.name: Interpreting Temperature Effects on Kc
concepts.explanation: Predicting how Kc changes with temperature for endothermic (K increases) and exothermic (K decreases) forward reactions.

concepts.name: Using ICE Tables in Equilibrium Problems
concepts.explanation: Setting up and populating Initial, Change, and Equilibrium rows to track concentration changes and form solvable equations.

concepts.name: pH as a Negative Logarithm
concepts.explanation: Defining pH by pH = −log10[H+], linking acidity to a logarithmic scale of hydrogen ion concentration.

concepts.name: Converting Between pH and [H+]
concepts.explanation: Using logarithms and antilogarithms to compute [H+] from pH and vice versa: [H+] = 10^(−pH).

concepts.name: Ionic Product of Water and pH–pOH Relation
concepts.explanation: Applying Kw = [H+][OH−] and at 25°C, pH + pOH = 14, to interconvert hydrogen and hydroxide concentrations.

concepts.name: Calculating pH of Strong Acids
concepts.explanation: Determining pH by assuming full dissociation and using stoichiometry to find [H+], then pH = −log10[H+].

concepts.name: Calculating pH of Strong Bases via pOH
concepts.explanation: Computing [OH−] from full dissociation, finding pOH = −log10[OH−], and then pH = 14 − pOH (at 25°C).

concepts.name: Weak Acid pH via Ka Square-Root Approximation
concepts.explanation: Using [H+] ≈ √(Ka·C) for weak acids at modest dilution when x ≪ C, then pH = −log10[H+].

concepts.name: Weak Base pH via Kb Square-Root Approximation
concepts.explanation: Using [OH−] ≈ √(Kb·C) for weak bases, then pOH = −log10[OH−] and pH = 14 − pOH (at 25°C).

concepts.name: Applying the Quadratic Formula in Equilibrium Calculations
concepts.explanation: Solving quadratic equations arising from exact equilibrium expressions when approximations are invalid.

concepts.name: Mass–Moles–Molarity Conversion
concepts.explanation: Converting between mass, moles, and concentration (mol/L) to prepare and analyze solutions.

concepts.name: Selecting Indicators by Matching pH Range to Titration Curve
concepts.explanation: Choosing an indicator whose color change range lies within the steep region around the equivalence point.

concepts.name: Identifying the Equivalence Point from a pH Titration Curve
concepts.explanation: Locating the point of stoichiometric neutralization using the inflection/steepest region on a pH vs. volume graph.

concepts.name: Interpreting the Logarithmic Nature of the pH Scale
concepts.explanation: Recognizing that a 1-unit change in pH corresponds to a tenfold change in [H+].

concepts.name: Two-Point Calibration of a pH Sensor with Buffers
concepts.explanation: Setting sensor response using two standard buffer solutions to achieve accurate pH measurements.

concepts.name: Predicting Pressure Effects by Comparing Gaseous Mole Counts
concepts.explanation: Using stoichiometric coefficients of gaseous species to infer volume change and equilibrium shift under pressure changes.

concepts.name: Interpreting Magnitude of Kc
concepts.explanation: Relating large Kc to product-favored equilibria and small Kc to reactant-favored equilibria to gauge reaction extent.

concepts.name: Biochemical Oxygen Demand Calculation with Dilution Factor
concepts.explanation: Compute BOD as the difference between initial and 5-day dissolved oxygen readings and scale by the dilution factor when the sample was diluted.

concepts.name: ppm–mg/L Conversion for Aqueous Solutions
concepts.explanation: Convert between parts per million (ppm) and mg/L for dilute water samples, using 1 ppm ≈ 1 mg/L.

concepts.name: Compound Percentage Calculation for Resource Availability
concepts.explanation: Calculate accessible fractions using successive percentages, e.g., 97% saltwater, 3% freshwater, two-thirds of which is inaccessible.

concepts.name: Exponential Growth from Annual Percentage Increase
concepts.explanation: Model quantities growing by a fixed percent per year, using compound growth to estimate future amounts (e.g., 4% per year).

concepts.name: Interpreting Time-Series Graphs with Seasonal Variation
concepts.explanation: Read trends and periodic patterns in time-series data such as atmospheric CO2 with seasonal oscillations.

concepts.name: Metric Unit Conversion: Micrometres to Metres
concepts.explanation: Convert micrometres (μm) to metres using 1 μm = 10^-6 m and perform related unit conversions.

concepts.name: Stoichiometric Ratio Calculation from Balanced Equations
concepts.explanation: Use coefficients in balanced chemical equations to determine mole ratios for quantitative reasoning.

concepts.name: Average Rate of Change from Experimental Data
concepts.explanation: Compute average rate as change in a measured quantity over time, e.g., oxygen consumption per day in BOD tests.

concepts.name: Comparing Relative Indices Using Global Warming Potential
concepts.explanation: Interpret and compare effects of gases via a relative index (GWP) referenced to CO2 = 1 using ratio reasoning.

concepts.name: Interpreting Percentage Contributions from Pie Charts
concepts.explanation: Extract and compare percentage shares from pie charts such as greenhouse gas contribution diagrams.

concepts.name: Calorimetry Energy Calculation (q = m c ΔT)
concepts.explanation: Compute heat exchanged using mass, specific heat capacity, and temperature change: q = m × c × (T2 − T1).

concepts.name: Molar Enthalpy from Experimental Heat
concepts.explanation: Scale measured heat for a sample to per-mole value by dividing by moles reacted to obtain kJ mol−1.

concepts.name: Hess's Law Equation Combination
concepts.explanation: Add, subtract, and scale thermochemical equations and their ΔH values to compute an unknown enthalpy change.

concepts.name: Bond Enthalpy Method for Reaction Enthalpy
concepts.explanation: Estimate ΔH using average bond enthalpies: ΔH = Σ(bonds broken) − Σ(bonds formed).

concepts.name: Stoichiometric Scaling of Enthalpy Change
concepts.explanation: Adjust ΔH proportionally when a thermochemical equation is multiplied or divided by a factor.

concepts.name: Converting Volume and Molarity to Moles (n = cV/1000)
concepts.explanation: Calculate moles of solute from solution volume (cm³) and concentration (mol L−1) via n = c × V/1000.

concepts.name: Using Density to Convert Volume to Mass (m = ρV)
concepts.explanation: Determine mass from volume using density, including water’s 1 g cm−3 to convert cm³ to g or kg.

concepts.name: Heat Capacity Calculation (Q = C ΔT)
concepts.explanation: Use system heat capacity C to compute heat change with Q = C × (T2 − T1) when c and mass are not used separately.

concepts.name: Unit Conversion in Thermochemistry
concepts.explanation: Convert among J and kJ, cm³ and kg, ensuring compatibility with specific heat capacity units.

concepts.name: Sign Convention for Enthalpy Change
concepts.explanation: Interpret ΔH < 0 as exothermic and ΔH > 0 as endothermic; apply correct sign in calculations and answers.

concepts.name: Interpreting kJ mol−1 Units
concepts.explanation: Understand enthalpy values as energy per mole of reaction as written, tied to the balanced equation stoichiometry.

concepts.name: Computing an Arithmetic Mean
concepts.explanation: Calculate average bond enthalpy by taking the mean of multiple bond dissociation energies.

concepts.name: Constructing Balanced Thermochemical Equations with States
concepts.explanation: Balance chemical equations and annotate physical states and ΔH, ensuring one-mole conventions when required.

concepts.name: Half-Reaction Method for Balancing Redox Equations
concepts.explanation: Balancing oxidation-reduction equations by writing separate oxidation and reduction half-reactions, equalizing electrons, and combining to obtain the net balanced equation.

concepts.name: Ordering Elements by Standard Electrode Potential
concepts.explanation: Interpreting and ranking elements using their standard electrode potentials to compare relative tendencies to be oxidized or reduced.

concepts.name: Predicting Metal Displacement Using the Electrochemical Series
concepts.explanation: Using the ordered list of standard electrode potentials to determine whether one metal will displace another from solution.

concepts.name: Stoichiometric Gas Volume Ratio from Balanced Equations
concepts.explanation: Using stoichiometric coefficients to predict gas volume ratios, e.g., electrolysis of water producing H2:O2 in a 2:1 ratio.

concepts.name: Summing Voltages in Series-Connected Cells
concepts.explanation: Computing total battery voltage by adding the voltages of individual cells connected in series, e.g., 4 × 1.5 V = 6 V.

concepts.name: Computing Fuel Cell Stack Voltage from Per-Cell Voltage and Cell Count
concepts.explanation: Calculating the output voltage of a fuel cell stack as the product of the number of cells and the single-cell voltage (e.g., 300–400 cells × 0.7 V).
